content.rationale:
The registry-side discard this unit's decision models is checked by running it: `specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt` imports the registry from `draft_state` (`specs/drafts/state.qnt`, tvtnokzu) and the discard from `specs/drafts/discard.qnt`, and it fixes the interface that module must carry - module `draft_discard`, `action discard(handles: List[str])` over the registry variable `records`, total over the handle list it is given: every call either removes exactly the records it names, each of them open, or is a whole-call refusal that leaves the registry as it was. The check reads no helper of the discard module and no field of the registry the state model does not already carry; it calls the one action and compares the registry before the call with the registry after it.

The check seeds a registry the prerequisites admit - three open drafts over two nodes and two landed records, each filed under its own handle through the state module's own constructor - and composes the discard into a step: every step records the registry as it stood and the handle list the call named, then runs `discard` over that list. The call pool covers the cases the prerequisites name: an empty call, one open handle, one landed handle, a handle the registry does not hold, two open handles, an open handle with a landed one, an open handle with an absent one, two landed handles, a handle named twice, and every open record. Four invariants are stated over each step. An accepted call - every handle it names picking out an open record - leaves exactly those records removed and nothing else (`SelectionIsExact`). Every record the call did not name stays at its handle field for field, and no unnamed record is dropped (`OthersUntouched`). A record that had landed before the call is still there, unchanged (`LandedNeverRemoved`). The registry after a call holds a subset of what it held before, so no record is added (`NoRecordAdded`). Six runs execute one case each and assert its outcome: one open record, two open records, a landed handle, an absent handle, an open handle with a landed one, and two landed handles.

Each prerequisite is used for one thing. slwvtspu fixes what a discard ends - an open draft, ended without landing - so the check lets a call name only a record that is still open and treats a landed record as no subject. lnpnkvkv fixes the selection and the refusal: the handles are the keys the call names, the subject set is the open records, and a call naming any handle that is not an open record is refused whole rather than answered in part; the check's acceptance condition is exactly that condition, and its no-record-added invariant is the invocation's no-node-no-change boundary read over the registry. yomurusp fixes the store side - exactly the named records' documents go, every other record stays at its handle, no landed record is ever removed, absence is no third state - which is the removal, retention and landed-end invariants together with the runs' handle-by-handle comparisons. tvtnokzu fixes the record's form, its two state values and the registry map the action steps; the check imports that module and restates none of it, so the record shape, the states and the content-identity base stay the state model's.

The change abandonment and the workspace forget a real discard performs are jj and filesystem effects and are outside this model: the check states nothing about them and neither invariant nor run constrains them.

The check is run mechanically. `quint typecheck specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt` first, for the grammar and the types; then `quint verify specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt --main=draft_discard_check --init=initCheck --backend=tlc --invariant=SelectionIsExact,OthersUntouched,LandedNeverRemoved,NoRecordAdded --max-steps=6`, the four invariants bounded-exhaustively over every trace to the bound; then `quint test specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt`, which executes the six runs. The module starts from its seeded registry rather than from the state module's empty `init`, so the verifier is given `--init=initCheck`; `--backend=tlc` keeps the run free of the Apalache flattening step, and `--backend=apalache` is the same check when a JDK is present.

The check tracks no wording of the decision. It fixes the action's contract - a call either removes exactly the open records it names or leaves the registry unchanged - which is what the decision models, so a rewording of the decision that leaves that contract unchanged leaves the check intact. The module and action names are the check's interface with the artifact, not a rule about how the discard is written inside it, and the seeded handles, node ids and bases are values the check chooses, none of them derived from a prerequisite. The node states no verdict: whether a particular artifact satisfies the check is a finding about a run, not content of this evaluation.
